groups.___: NAMING v2 ADDITIONS (docs namesystemv2g) — pools + filters the v2 template sets require. Direct-address, solo-act nickname/honorific, band groupNoun filters, jazz/easy adjectives, regional/abstract domains.

groups.//: === REGIONAL — place names (easy/blues/jazz reference 'regional'; was undefined = hard fail). ===
=== OPENERS — sentence-initial hooks. Sub-tagged by intent so genre + punctuation post-proc can select register. Gender-neutral. ===
=== LOVE / ADDRESS TERMS — the 'you' being sung to. Gender-soft; adapter may gender-agree. ===
=== PHRASE FRAGMENTS — parenthetical subtitles (Motown/soul/easy signature). Full clauses used inside (...). ===

=== formerly the pool behind 'easy_journey' ('%noun% (%phraseFrag%)') — that construction is retired per the doc (parentheses aren't automatically instrumental); folded into the instrumentalTitle system instead of going unused. ===

=== NICKNAMES — split into blues' real grammatical classes (doc: 'Little Walter' is prefix+first name, 'Lightnin' Hopkins' is epithet+surname, 'Howlin' Wolf' is a complete stage name; a single unrestricted pool produces 'Howlin' Johnson'/'Guitar Hopkins'). stagePrefix moved to the honorific pool below. ===

=== 'Some historical jazz nicknames were highly individual and should not be treated as generic reusable prefixes' (doc) — split into surnameEpithet (Dizzy Gillespie shape) and personalEpithet (rarer, more idiosyncratic); Duke/Count/Satchmo/Lady moved to the stageName pool below as complete units. ===

=== 'Little'/'Big' moved to the honorific pool as stagePrefix (they precede a first name); this pool is now personalEpithet-only (replaces the first name or precedes a surname) — the exact split the doc calls for, since mixing them produced 'Fats Richard'/'Little Domino'. ===

=== 'Cowboy'/'Little Jimmy' moved to the honorific pool as stagePrefix (they precede a first name); this pool is personalEpithet-only (Tex Ritter shape: epithet replaces/precedes the surname), same split rationale as doo-wop/soul/rock-and-roll. ===
=== HONORIFICS — carry male/female gender tags for the genderAgree constraint (Phase B). ===

=== INSTRUMENTS — split by class (doc: 'and His %instrument%' was too literal on its own; '[Name] at the Organ'/'Plays the Trumpet' need keyboard vs. featuredSolo vs. orchestralSection distinctions). ===
=== NUMBERS — garage/funk numeric titles. 'small' for (Part N). ===
=== FILM TITLES — soundtrack pseudo-titles. Evocative fake movie names. ===
=== nounAbs — abstract/uncountable concepts for '...of Freedom' frames (doowop/soul). ===
=== ADJECTIVES — moods the v2 templates filter on that had almost no coverage. ===
=== GROUPNOUN FILTERS — band-suffix pools the v2 band templates need (were failing silently). ===

groups.___: DOOWOP v2 additions (naming-genre-templates directive): vocal-group emblem nouns, a purpose-built/place-derived groupNoun pool, vocable/title-clause phraseFrags, transitivity-tagged verbs, and the small new pos categories (adverb/questionWord/personNoun) doo-wop's syntactic titles need.

groups.//: === VOCAL-GROUP EMBLEM NOUNS — the bird/gem/celestial/status pools period groups actually drew their names from (Orioles, Ravens, Flamingos, Diamonds...). Tagged 'vocalGroup' so The %noun:pl% stops being celestial/gem-only. ===
=== NUMBERED VOCAL GROUPS — group-level 'weight' skews the draw toward Five/Four over Six/Three (doc: period groups were overwhelmingly named Four/Five). ===
=== PURPOSE-BUILT / PLACE-DERIVED groupNoun — invented plural collectives, distinct from the gems/birds/royalty/musical pools (which doo-wop bands also drew from via the OR filter). ===

=== STAGE-PREFIX HONORIFICS — 'Little'/'Baby'/'Junior' as a grammatical class distinct from a personal nickname (Fats, Muddy). Tagged with the real 'early60s' era class so they fade on schedule rather than a fake era tag. ===
=== ADJECTIVES — color/youthful, for the collective + celestial title constructions. ===
=== TITLE-CLAUSE / VOCABLE / RESPONSE phraseFrags — curated whole units, not Markov-generated (doo-wop's vocables and complete-clause titles need to read as real phrases, not noun-salad). ===

=== VERBS — transitivity/register tags (doowop's direct-address grammar needs 'takes a person object' vs 'stands alone' as an explicit distinction, not just mood). Layered atop existing mood tags via domain tags (romance/emotion). ===
=== NEW POS CATEGORIES — small curated pools for grammatical slots doo-wop's constructions need that no existing pos covers. ===

=== NOUNS — the remaining grammatical/domain tags the fixed song-title constructions need (stillness-of-night, noun-on-my-noun, book-of-love, my-love, single-word). Small curated pools, not the broad celestial/romance sweep the old templates over-relied on. ===
